repo_prior_art.cite: stat_transported_late_strength_frontier — weak-IV confidence-set frontier, not a continuous polynomial-boundary transported-mean risk theorem.

published_prior_art.cite: KhanTamer2010 gives irregular inverse-weight rates; ZhangLiuWangTeng2025 gives covariate-shift moment bounds on a different bounded-ratio Sobolev model.
BurmanGamaloGhosalKundu2026 develops regular bounded-overlap RiCOT; OriharaKomukaiLi2026 is one-sample observational limited-propensity extrapolation.

repo_prior_art.cite: stat_transported_late_strength_frontier concerns finite-cell transported IV strength rather than this Hölder boundary-overlap phase diagram.

published_prior_art.cite: No verified paper gives the claimed two-sample polynomial-source-boundary frontier, including the critical a=1 logarithm.
ArmstrongKolesar2020 supplies bias-aware local-polynomial intervals and MaWang2020 supplies weak-overlap IPW inference, but neither gives this learned two-sample transport process.
CaiLow2004 supplies the ordered-modulus framework but not this weighted transported-functional modulus.
Bull2012 treats self-similar function bands under regular observation norms, not joint (a,s) adaptation for a two-sample transported functional.

novelty_flags.label: thm:sharp-frontier; related_work; comparator_promise_table
novelty_flags.one_line: BurmanGamaloGhosalKundu2026 does not cover the proposal's covariate-only target-sample ATE at a=0: its target sample includes treated outcomes and its estimand uses the target treated mean plus a transported trial control regression, so the claimed covered endpoint/strict relaxation is not a like-for-like comparator.

soundness_flags.label: def:ricot-weights; def:spliced-estimator; thm:ricot-attainment
soundness_flags.one_line: The fold-trained RiCOT density is explicitly defined only on the training source empirical support and as zero elsewhere, but is evaluated on independent held-out source observations; no out-of-sample weight extension is constructed.

soundness_flags.label: thm:ricot-attainment; thm:sharp-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: Under the displayed construction the held-out residual correction is almost surely zero for continuous X, leaving a target plug-in spline estimator; hence the asserted a=0 root-rate attainment and its claimed regular-endpoint reduction do not follow from this procedure.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The frontier is conditional on the one-dimensional polynomial source-boundary class, bounded outcomes, known randomized propensity, and prespecified regularity indices.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Any repaired sharp frontier is only over this factorized one-dimensional transport class, not multivariate boundaries or observational assignment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:fixed-class-honesty and oeq:self-similar-adaptation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Fixed-class inference prespecifies (a,s,t,M); joint adaptation is confined to the stated self-similar subclass and remains open.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Honesty is fixed-class; no unrestricted adaptation claim is accepted.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper observes target O_j^Q=(X_j^Q,Y_j^Q) with treated target outcomes, identifies tau_Q=E_Q[Y^Q]-E_Q[mu_0(X^Q)], and gives an influence function with a target treated-outcome component and a transported trial-control-residual component; Assumption 1(iv) requires bounded dQ_X/dP_X.
The article connects arbitrarily large identifying inverse weights with irregular, tail-dependent slower-than-parametric estimation and includes an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Theorem 1; pp. 5 and 24–25, two-stage and likelihood-ratio sections
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves a lower bound for q-th moments under covariate shift and develops a two-stage likelihood-ratio-calibrated estimator; it is not a transported causal trial-effect theorem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–3, Abstract and Introduction; pp. 4–6, setup
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a one-sample observational ATE with limited treatment-propensity overlap, using beta-weighted estimand trajectories and polynomial extrapolation under an ignorable approximation-bias condition.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 115(532), version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies robust trimmed-IPW inference under small denominators and different asymptotic regimes.
The paper develops honest scalar nonparametric-regression intervals based on local-polynomial estimators and bias-aware critical values.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author-accessible version of Annals of Statistics 32(5) article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article characterizes adaptive confidence intervals for linear functionals using between-class and ordered moduli.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1110.4985, published in Electronic Journal of Statistics 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article establishes self-similarity conditions for honest adaptive confidence bands over Hölder classes in regular density, regression, and white-noise models.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the empirical-support weight with a fold-trained measurable out-of-sample function, for example by defining and evaluating the calibrated dual-potential/exponential-tilt extension; alternatively abandon weight cross-fitting and formulate the needed same-sample empirical-process control explicitly.

Recast the Burman comparison as informed-by, or modify the observed-data configuration and estimand so that the a=0 theorem is genuinely nested in BurmanGamaloGhosalKundu2026 before claiming a strict overlap relaxation.
After repairing the estimator, add a dedicated a=0 corollary that writes its residual term and verifies the root-rate reduction directly under the repaired construction.

recommended_next_step: Reject this version and return to Stage -1 for a repaired out-of-sample RiCOT construction and a source-faithful comparator claim; the polynomial-boundary frontier itself remains a plausible field-tier research kernel after those repairs.
